c.tagline: A living Silk Road museum of madrasas, minarets and turquoise domes.

taxi.fareNote: Street taxis are unmarked and unmetered — agree the fare before getting in, or book a fixed price through Yandex Go.

emergency.note: Fire is 101 and gas emergencies are 104; 112 also works as a general emergency line.

avoid.reason: Nothing beyond bazaar overcharging and taxi haggling — agree prices before setting off.

hood_desc: The walkable heart of the old town, wrapped around the Lyab-i Hauz pool and its shaded chaikhanas, madrasas and the Nadir Divan-Begi ensemble; the natural base for first-timers with everything within a few minutes' stroll.

The monumental core around the Po-i-Kalyan complex — the towering 12th-century Kalyan Minaret, Kalyan Mosque and Mir-i-Arab Madrasa — plus the covered trading domes (taqi) and Ulugh Beg and Abdulaziz Khan madrasas; the densest concentration of Bukhara's UNESCO sights.

The area facing the massive Ark fortress and Bukhara's own Registan square, taking in the Bolo Hauz Mosque with its carved wooden columns; a monument-heavy quarter that shows off the emirs' seat of power.
The atmospheric old Jewish mahalla of narrow lanes and traditional courtyard houses near Lyab-i Hauz, home to a historic synagogue; a quiet, authentic pocket of everyday Bukhara.

A greener, calmer western district around Samanid Recreation Park, the 10th-century Ismail Samani Mausoleum and the Chashma-Ayub shrine; relaxed and residential with space to breathe away from the bazaar crowds.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; the tap supply is not reliable for visitors.

transit.hours: City buses and marshrutka minibuses run roughly 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM; Yandex Go and street taxis cover late-night trips.
transit.note: Bukhara has no metro or tram. The UNESCO old town is small and best explored on foot; buses, marshrutkas and cheap taxis link the historic core with the newer districts and the railway station at nearby Kagan.
transit.pay: Bus and marshrutka fares are paid in cash to the driver (around 1,700 so'm); taxis are cheap but unmetered, so agree the price first or use Yandex Go. There is no rechargeable transit card.

bus: Intercity buses & shared taxis to Samarkand, Khiva/Urgench and Tashkent
train: Afrosiyob high-speed & Sharq trains (Bukhara / Kagan station) to Samarkand and Tashkent

transit.m: City bus / marshrutka to the old town (~20-30 min)
Taxi or Yandex Go to the center (10-15 min)

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up or leaving 5-10% for good service at tourist restaurants is appreciated.
